duel.summary: Restored duel-online-001's snapshot (git restore from refs/workflow/9d324071c360f7c2/duel, ':!features'; diff against the ref was empty afterwards, and every restored path is owned). Then fixed findings 1-8. (1) apps/web/src/devLatency.ts exports DelayLine with an injectable clock and random source (no DOM). Unit tests use fake timers and a real SDK Room on a stand-in socket. They check the RTT/2 delay each way, the ±jitter/2 bound, and that probes, inputs and bundles are never reordered. Mutating the delay, the jitter or the ordering fails them. New tests/integration/devLatency.test.ts wraps two HeadlessDuelClients in applyDevLatency: room RTT went from about 2 to 81 ms and input delay from 3 to 6, with 0 desyncs. (2) New pure inputDelayFromSamples (used by DuelRoom) has exact-value unit tests. The harness asserts that both delays are within 3..8 and that the impaired delay is higher (3 vs 8 in the run). (3) The HUD's stamina is checked in a unit test (renderDuelHud on a fake root) and in the duel-practice browser scenario (Shift dash: 80 and 80%). (4) The resync test now asserts that the confirmed state equals the authority's. A new hidden-tab test sends contiguous bundles while ticks stall. (5) New tests: a KO re-simulated by a correction is reported once, and a view-side test shows PendingDuelEvents and ArenaFlashes (new apps/web/src/duelEvents.ts, used by DuelClient and ArenaScene) draw each id once. (6) DuelRoom queues forfeits and resolves them together at the next frame boundary. One forfeit means the opponent wins. Two on the same frame means winner -1, reason forfeit ('Both forfeit: no winner'). Integration tests cover a staggered double drop, where the first to expire forfeits, and both expiries in either order. (7) DuelRollback.canStep stops at a frame with a result. DuelClientSession.finish() steps to the last bundle's frame once the phase is over, in both the browser and the headless client, with a unit test. (8) InputGate and DuelInputGate share InputAdmission (rate window plus validation). InputGate's tests are unchanged, and a new test shows that both gates drop the same messages. Docs (duel.md, architecture.md) are updated. Checks run in this worktree after npm ci: npm run typecheck (0), npm run test:unit (341/341), npm run test:integration (36/36, 137 s), npm run build including smoke (0), and the full Playwright suite (6/6). The JSON report passed the pinned check-report for all six scenarios.
open_assumptions: A double forfeit is represented as winner -1 with reason 'forfeit'. No new end reason was added and PROTOCOL_VERSION is unchanged. The standalone duel room has no rewards, so 'rewards cancelled' only means that no winner is recorded (documented in docs/duel.md).

The same-frame double-forfeit integration test drops both players for real, then calls DuelRoom.onLeave for both seats in one synchronous block, in each order. This is what Colyseus does when both reconnection timers fire in the same tick. Real timers are not forced onto one frame.
Prediction now also stops at a predicted result, not only a confirmed one, and resumes if a correction takes the result back (unit-tested). This changes the shared rollback core's behaviour.
The duel gate's rate window now starts at tick 0 like the world gate's, instead of at the first message. This only changes the first second of a room.
ArenaFlashes keeps its own memory of the last 64 ids on top of DuelEventFeed's de-duplication.
